reason: E1 and E2 directly support the role of limited mobility in forming mixed nanoparticles from solid precursors. E3 provides direct evidence for strong anchoring and thermal stability on defective T-graphite supports. The boundary condition regarding high-mobility synthesis is implied by E1's contrast with solution-based methods. The combined mechanism of low-temperature synthesis plus support anchoring is a synthesis of these separate findings, not a single directly tested claim.
premises: Limited atomic mobility during low-temperature synthesis from solid precursors promotes a random, mixed state in multi-element nanoparticles
Strong interfacial binding to defect/edge sites on a support (e.g., T-graphite) anchors nanoparticles and retards atomic diffusion
This anchoring prevents phase separation and coarsening at high service temperatures (773–1923 K)
The stabilization effect is diminished when synthesis involves high atomic mobility (e.g., solution-based methods)
